Notes on efficient dominating sets and efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphsThanks:   This research is supported by National Natural Science Foundation of China (Nos. 11401368 and 12326333)

Yun-Ping Deng Affiliation: Department of Mathematics, Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai 201306, China    Xuanlong Ma Note: Corresponding author Affiliation: School of Science, Xi’an Petroleum University, Xi’an 710065, China
Abstract

Let DD be a proper subset of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n} such that |D||D| divides nn and is relatively prime to n|D|\frac{n}{|D|}. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for DD to be an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S). Moreover, for an inverse-closed subset SS of ℤn∖{0}\mathbb{Z}_{n}\setminus\{0\} such that |S|+1|S|+1 divides nn and is relatively prime to n|S|+1\frac{n}{|S|+1}, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets in Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S). We also obtain some results about the set of all efficient dominating sets in any circulant graph. Similar results for efficient open dominating sets are also obtained. These results extend some theorems in [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1503–1507], [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1522–1527], and [Des. Codes Cryptogr. 94 (2026), 87].

Key words: Circulant graph; Cayley graph; Efficient dominating set; Efficient open dominating set

AMS Classifications: 05C25, 05C69

1 Introduction

Let GG be a finite group with identity element ee and SS an inverse-closed subset of GG not containing e.e. The Cayley graph on GG with respect to the connection set SS is defined as the graph with vertex set GG and edge set {{g,sg}:g∈G,s∈S}\{\{g,sg\}\colon\,g{\in}G,\ s{\in}S\} and denoted by Cay​(G,S).\hbox{\rm Cay}(G,S). A Cayley graph on finite cyclic group ℤn:={0,1,⋯,n−1}\mathbb{Z}_{n}:=\{0,1,\cdots,n-1\} with addition modulo nn is called a circulant graph.

A subset DD of vertices in a graph Γ\Gamma is called an efficient dominating set (also called a perfect code) if DD is an independent set and each vertex not in DD is adjacent to exactly one vertex in D.D. By the definitions of a circulant graph and an efficient dominating set, it is easy to see that if Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set D,D, then n=(|S|+1)​|D|.n=(|S|+1)|D|. A subset DD of vertices in a graph Γ\Gamma is called an efficient open dominating set (also called a total perfect code) if each vertex in Γ\Gamma is adjacent to exactly one vertex in D.D. Similarly, one can easily see that if Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient open dominating set D,D, then n=|S|​|D|,n=|S||D|, and DD induces a matching in Cay​(ℤn,S),\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S), which implies that |D||D| is even.

The existence of efficient dominating sets in some families of graphs was first studied by Biggs [1] and Kratochvíl [9]. It was proved in [11] that a Cayley graph on an abelian group admits an efficient dominating set if and only if it is a covering graph of a complete graph. In [3], a method for constructing E-chains of Cayley graphs was given and was used to construct infinite families of E-chains of Cayley graphs on symmetric groups, where an E-chain is a countable family of nested graphs each containing an efficient dominating set. In [14], Terada showed that there exists no efficient dominating set in any Cayley graph on special linear group SL​(2,2f)​(f>1)\hbox{\rm SL}(2,2^{f})~(f>1) with respect to a conjugation-closed connection set.

During the past two decades, efficient dominating sets in circulant graphs have attracted considerable attention. For example, Kumar and MacGillivray [10] characterized the efficient dominating sets in circulant graphs with domination number two and three, and Deng [4] further characterized the existence and construction of efficient dominating sets with domination number prime. In [12], Obradović, Peters and Ružić gave necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of efficient dominating sets in connected circulant graphs of degree 33 and 4.4. Applying the tool of cyclotomic polynomials, Feng et al. [7] generalized the results in [12] by considering the case of degree pl−1p^{l}-1 (pp prime and ll positive integer). Almost at the same time, using the subset direct sum method, Deng et al. [5] independently gave necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of efficient dominating sets in connected non-complete circulant graphs Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) of degree |S|=p−1,p​q−1|S|=p-1,pq-1 and pm−1p^{m}-1 (p,qp,q primes and mm positive integer) or order n=pk​q,p2​q2,p​q​r,p2​q​r,p​q​r​sn=p^{k}q,p^{2}q^{2},pqr,p^{2}qr,pqrs (p,q,r,sp,q,r,s distinct primes and kk positive integer) satisfying that |S|+1|S|+1 divides nn and |S|+1|S|+1 is relatively prime to n|S|+1.\frac{n}{|S|+1}. Efficient open dominating sets have also received much attention in recent years. In [8, Corollary 3.5 (b)], Huang et al. gave a necessary and sufficient condition for a subgroup to be an efficient open dominating set in circulant graphs. Feng et al. [7] gave a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient open dominating sets in connected circulant graphs Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) of degree |S|=pl|S|=p^{l} (pp prime and ll positive integer) satisfying that |S||S| divides nn and |S||S| is relatively prime to n|S|\frac{n}{|S|}. In terms of the order of a cyclic group and the cardinality of an efficient dominating set (resp. an efficient open dominating set), Feng et al. [6] gave a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets (resp. efficient open dominating sets) in circulant graphs. Wang et al. [16] studied efficient dominating sets in circulant graphs of degree pl−1p^{l}-1, where pp is a prime and l≥1l\geq 1, which extended known results in [7] and provided insight on the general problem on the existence and structure of efficient dominating sets in circulant graphs. Recently, Cameron et al. [2] generalized some results in [7] to general abelian groups.

In this note, we generalize the results in [2], [5], and [7] by proving that the similar result holds for any circulant graph Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) of general degree |S||S| and general order nn satisfying that |S|+1|S|+1 divides nn and |S|+1|S|+1 is relatively prime to n|S|+1.\frac{n}{|S|+1}. Furthermore, for any circulant graph which admits an efficient dominating set, the present paper gives some results about the set of all its efficient dominating sets. We further give a necessary and sufficient condition for a general subset to be an efficient dominating set in circulant graphs. Similar results for efficient open dominating sets are also obtained.

2 Preliminaries

Let GG be a finite abelian group with additive notation, and let M,NM,N be two subsets of GG . If every g∈Gg\in G has a unique representation in the form g=m+ng=m+n with m∈M,n∈Nm\in M,n\in N, then GG is called the direct sum of MM and NN. In this case, we write G=M⊕NG=M\oplus N. For two positive integers m,nm,n, we use (m,n)(m,n) to denote the greatest common divisor of mm and nn. If (m,n)=1(m,n)=1, then mm and nn are relatively prime.

Proposition 2.1

([15, Proposition 2.1]) Let GG be a finite abelian group and let M,NM,N be subsets of GG . Then G=M⊕NG=M\oplus N is equivalent to the conjunction of any two of the following conditions:

  • (i)

    G=M+NG=M+N;

  • (ii)

    (M−M)∩(N−N)={0}(M-M)\cap(N-N)=\{0\};

  • (ii)

    |G|=|M|​|N||G|=|M||N|.

If SS is a subset of a finite abelian group GG, then we write S0=S∪{0}S_{0}=S\cup\{0\}.

Lemma 2.2

([4, Lemma 2.3]) A subset DD of finite abelian group GG is an efficient dominating set of Cay​(G,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(G,S) if and only if G=S0⊕DG=S_{0}\oplus D.

For any subset MM of an abelian group G,G, the set of all g∈Gg\in G satisfying g+M=Mg+M=M is a subgroup of GG , called the stability subgroup of M,M, denoted by GM.G_{M}. It is easy to see that MM is a union of cosets of GM.G_{M}. Moreover, if 0∈M,0\in M, then GM⊆M.G_{M}\subseteq M. A subset M⊆GM\subseteq G is called periodic if GM≠{0}.G_{M}\neq\{0\}. Otherwise, a subset M⊆GM\subseteq G is called aperiodic if GM={0}.G_{M}=\{0\}.

Lemma 2.3

([4, Lemma 2.4]) Let SS and DD be two subsets of finite abelian group GG , and let A=GS0A=G_{S_{0}}. Then G=S0⊕DG=S_{0}\oplus D if and only if G/A=S0/A⊕(D+A)/AG/A=S_{0}/A\oplus(D+A)/A and A∩(D−D)={0}A\cap(D-D)=\{0\}.

Lemma 2.4

([13, Theorem 3.17]) Let GG be a finite abelian group, and let M,NM,N be subsets of GG . If G=M⊕N,G=M\oplus N, then G=k​M⊕NG=kM\oplus N for any integer kk relatively prime to |M|,|M|, where k​M={k​m:m∈M}.kM=\{km\colon\,m\in M\}.

The following result was first stated in [12, Remark 1] and also appears in [4].

Lemma 2.5

([12, Remark 1]) Let n=|S0|​d,n=|S_{0}|d, where dd is an integer. Then Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set DD which is a coset of some subgroup of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n} if and only if s−s′≢0​(m​o​d​|S0|)s-s^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|S_{0}|) for any distinct s,s′∈S0,s,s^{\prime}\in S_{0}, where S0=S∪{0}.S_{0}=S\cup\{0\}.

By the definitions of a Cayley graph and an efficient open dominating set, similar to Lemma 2.2, one can easily obtain the following result.

Lemma 2.6

A subset DD of a finite abelian group GG is an efficient open dominating set of Cay​(G,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(G,S) if and only if G=S⊕D.G=S\oplus D.

Similar to Lemma 2.5, we have the following result.

Lemma 2.7

Let n=|S|​d,n=|S|d, where dd is an integer. Then Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient open dominating set DD which is a coset of some subgroup of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n} if and only if s−s′≢0​(m​o​d​|S|)s-s^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|S|) for any distinct s,s′∈S.s,s^{\prime}\in S.

3 Efficient dominating sets

Clearly, if Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set DD, then n=(|S|+1)​|D|n=(|S|+1)|D|. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for a proper subset DD of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n} with |D||n|D|\mid n and (|D|,n|D|)=1(|D|,\frac{n}{|D|})=1 to be an efficient dominating set of Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S).

Theorem 3.1

Let DD be a proper subset of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n} such that |D||D| divides nn and is relatively prime to n|D|\frac{n}{|D|}. Then DD is an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) if and only if d−d′≢0​(m​o​d​|D|)d-d^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|D|) for distinct d,d′∈Dd,d^{\prime}\in D.

Proof. Suppose that d−d′≢0​(m​o​d​|D|)d-d^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|D|) for distinct d,d′∈Dd,d^{\prime}\in D. Then

(|D|​ℤn−|D|​ℤn)∩(D−D)={0}.(|D|\mathbb{Z}_{n}-|D|\mathbb{Z}_{n})\cap(D-D)=\{0\}.

Note that the cardinality of |D|​ℤn|D|\mathbb{Z}_{n} is n|D|.\frac{n}{|D|}. Therefore, by Proposition 2.1, ℤn=|D|​ℤn⊕D.\mathbb{Z}_{n}=|D|\mathbb{Z}_{n}\oplus D. Now let S=|D|​ℤn∖{0}.S=|D|\mathbb{Z}_{n}\setminus\{0\}. Then SS is inverse-closed and ℤn=S0⊕D,\mathbb{Z}_{n}=S_{0}\oplus D, where S0=S∪{0}.S_{0}=S\cup\{0\}. By Lemma 2.2, DD is an efficient dominating set in Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S), as desired.

Conversely, suppose that DD is an efficient dominating set in Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S). Then by Lemma 2.2, ℤn=S0⊕D,\mathbb{Z}_{n}=S_{0}\oplus D, where S0=S∪{0}.S_{0}=S\cup\{0\}. Set |S0|=k.|S_{0}|=k. Then n=k​|D|n=k|D| and kk is relatively prime to |D|.|D|. It follows from Lemma 2.4 that ℤn=S0⊕k​D,\mathbb{Z}_{n}=S_{0}\oplus kD, which implies that |k​D|=|D|.|kD|=|D|. Now we claim that d−d′≢0​(m​o​d​|D|)d-d^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|D|) for any distinct d,d′∈D.d,d^{\prime}\in D. Otherwise, if there exist some distinct d,d′∈Dd,d^{\prime}\in D such that d−d′≡0​(m​o​d​|D|),d-d^{\prime}\equiv 0~(mod~|D|), then k​d−k​d′≡0​(m​o​d​k​|D|),kd-kd^{\prime}\equiv 0~(mod~k|D|), that is, k​d−k​d′≡0​(m​o​d​n).kd-kd^{\prime}\equiv 0~(mod~n). Therefore, k​dkd and k​d′kd^{\prime} are the same element in ℤn,\mathbb{Z}_{n}, and thus |k​D|<|D|,|kD|<|D|, which is a contradiction.  

If SS is an inverse-closed subset of ℤn∖{0}\mathbb{Z}_{n}\setminus\{0\} such that (|S|+1)|n(|S|+1)\mid n and (|S|+1,n|S|+1)=1(|S|+1,\frac{n}{|S|+1})=1, then the following result gives a necessary and sufficient condition for which Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set.

Theorem 3.2

Let SS be an inverse-closed subset of ℤn∖{0}\mathbb{Z}_{n}\setminus\{0\} such that |S|+1|S|+1 divides nn and is relatively prime to n|S|+1\frac{n}{|S|+1}. Then Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set if and only if s−s′≢0​(m​o​d​|S0|)s-s^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|S_{0}|) for distinct s,s′∈S0.s,s^{\prime}\in S_{0}.

Proof. If s−s′≢0​(m​o​d​|S0|)s-s^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|S_{0}|) for distinct s,s′∈S0,s,s^{\prime}\in S_{0}, then by Lemma 2.5, Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set.

For the converse, suppose that Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set DD. Then by Lemma 2.2, ℤn=S0⊕D.\mathbb{Z}_{n}=S_{0}\oplus D. Set |D|=k.|D|=k. Then n=|S0|​kn=|S_{0}|k and kk is relatively prime to |S0|.|S_{0}|. It follows from Lemma 2.4 that ℤn=k​S0⊕D,\mathbb{Z}_{n}=kS_{0}\oplus D, which implies |k​S0|=|S0|.|kS_{0}|=|S_{0}|. Now we claim that s−s′≢0​(m​o​d​|S0|)s-s^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|S_{0}|) for any distinct s,s′∈S0.s,s^{\prime}\in S_{0}. Otherwise, if there exist some distinct s,s′∈S0s,s^{\prime}\in S_{0} such that s−s′≡0​(m​o​d​|S0|),s-s^{\prime}\equiv 0~(mod~|S_{0}|), then k​s−k​s′≡0​(m​o​d​k​|S0|),ks-ks^{\prime}\equiv 0~(mod~k|S_{0}|), that is, k​s−k​s′≡0​(m​o​d​n).ks-ks^{\prime}\equiv 0~(mod~n). Therefore, k​sks and k​s′ks^{\prime} are the same element in ℤn,\mathbb{Z}_{n}, and thus |k​S0|<|S0|,|kS_{0}|<|S_{0}|, which is a contradiction.  

In Theorem 3.2, if |S|=pl−1|S|=p^{l}-1 with pl|np^{l}\mid n and pl+1∤np^{l+1}\nmid n where pp is a prime and ll is a positive integer, then (pl,npl)=1(p^{l},\frac{n}{p^{l}})=1. Thus, Theorem 3.2 implies [7, Theorem 1.2]. Moreover, Theorem 3.2 also generalizes [5, Theorem 3.5].

Now by Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 3.2, one can easily observe the following result.

Corollary 3.3

Let SS be an inverse-closed subset of ℤn∖{0}\mathbb{Z}_{n}\setminus\{0\} such that |S|+1|S|+1 divides nn and is relatively prime to n|S|+1.\frac{n}{|S|+1}. Then Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set if and only if it admits an efficient dominating set that is a subgroup of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n}. In particular, if Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set, then every coset of the unique subgroup of order n|S|+1\frac{n}{|S|+1} in ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n} is an efficient dominating set.

The following theorem gives a complete structural description of efficient dominating sets in Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S), where |S|+1|S|+1 divides nn and is relatively prime to n|S|+1\frac{n}{|S|+1}.

Suppose that Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set. By Lemma 2.2, |S0|​ℤn∈𝔻.|S_{0}|\mathbb{Z}_{n}\in\mathbb{D}. On the other hand, for any D∈𝔻,D\in\mathbb{D}, by Theorem 3.1, d≢d′​(m​o​d​|D|)d\nequiv d^{\prime}~(mod~|D|) for any distinct d,d′∈D.d,d^{\prime}\in D. Since |D|=n|S0|,|D|=\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}, we may write D={d0,d1,⋯,dn|S0|−1}D=\{d_{0},d_{1},\cdots,d_{\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}-1}\} such that di≡i⁡(m​o​d​n|S0|)d_{i}\equiv i~(mod~\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}) for each i∈{0,1,⋯,n|S0|−1},i\in\{0,1,\cdots,\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}-1\}, and thus di=i+ki​n|S0|,d_{i}=i+k_{i}\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}, where ki∈{0,1,⋯,|S0|−1}.k_{i}\in\{0,1,\cdots,|S_{0}|-1\}. Hence 𝔻⊆{{i+kin|S0|:i=0,1,⋯,n|S0|−1}:∀ki∈{0,1,⋯,|S0|−1}}.\mathbb{D}\subseteq\{\{i+k_{i}\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}\colon\,i=0,1,\cdots,\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}-1\}\colon\,\forall\,k_{i}\in\{0,1,\cdots,|S_{0}|-1\}\}.

The following theorem extends the previous results to a more general setting and reduces the efficient domination problem in ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n} to the corresponding problem in the quotient group.

Theorem 3.5

Let SS be an inverse-closed subset of ℤn∖{0}\mathbb{Z}_{n}\setminus\{0\} such that |S|+1|S|+1 divides nn, and let m=(|S0|,n|S0|)m=(|S_{0}|,\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}). If (|S0|m,n|S0|)=1(\frac{|S_{0}|}{m},\frac{n}{|S_{0}|})=1, S0S_{0} is periodic with stability subgroup AA such that |A|=m,|A|=m, set S0/A={A,t1+A,⋯,t|S0|m−1+A}S_{0}/A=\{A,t_{1}+A,\cdots,t_{\frac{|S_{0}|}{m}-1}+A\} and T0={t0,t1,⋯,t|S0|m−1}T_{0}=\{t_{0},t_{1},\cdots,t_{\frac{|S_{0}|}{m}-1}\} where t0=0t_{0}=0 and 1≤ti≤nm−11\leq t_{i}\leq\frac{n}{m}-1 for i∈{1,⋯,|S0|m−1},i\in\{1,\cdots,\frac{|S_{0}|}{m}-1\}, then Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set if and only if t−t′≢0​(m​o​d​|S0|m)t-t^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~\frac{|S_{0}|}{m}) for distinct t,t′∈T0.t,t^{\prime}\in T_{0}.

Proof. If Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set D,D, then by Lemmas 2.2 and 2.3, ℤn=S0⊕D,\mathbb{Z}_{n}=S_{0}\oplus D, and thus ℤn/A=S0/A⊕(D+A)/A,A∩(D−D)={0},\mathbb{Z}_{n}/A=S_{0}/A\oplus(D+A)/A,\,A\cap(D-D)=\{0\}, it follows that Cay​(ℤn/A,S0/A∖{A})\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n}/A,S_{0}/A\setminus\{A\}) admits an efficient dominating set (D+A)/A,(D+A)/A, that is, Cay​(ℤnm,T0∖{0})\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{\frac{n}{m}},T_{0}\setminus\{0\}) admits an efficient dominating set. Since |T0|=|S0|m|T_{0}|=\frac{|S_{0}|}{m} and nm|T0|=n|S0|,\frac{\frac{n}{m}}{|T_{0}|}=\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}, it follows that |T0||T_{0}| is relatively prime to nm|T0|.\frac{\frac{n}{m}}{|T_{0}|}. By Theorem 3.2, t−t′≢0​(m​o​d​|S0|m)t-t^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~\frac{|S_{0}|}{m}) for any distinct t,t′∈T0.t,t^{\prime}\in T_{0}.

If t−t′≢0​(m​o​d​|S0|m)t-t^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~\frac{|S_{0}|}{m}) for any distinct t,t′∈T0,t,t^{\prime}\in T_{0}, then by Theorem 3.2, Cay​(ℤnm,T0∖{0})\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{\frac{n}{m}},T_{0}\setminus\{0\}) admits an efficient dominating set, that is, Cay​(ℤn/A,S0/A∖{A})\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n}/A,S_{0}/A\setminus\{A\}) admits an efficient dominating set, denoted by (D+A)/A.(D+A)/A. Set (D+A)/A={d1+A,⋯,dn|S0|+A}(D+A)/A=\{d_{1}+A,\cdots,d_{\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}}+A\} and set D={d1,⋯,dn|S0|}.D=\{d_{1},\cdots,d_{\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}}\}. By Lemma 2.2, ℤn/A=S0/A⊕(D+A)/A.\mathbb{Z}_{n}/A=S_{0}/A\oplus(D+A)/A. Since |(D+A)/A|=|D|=n|S0|,|(D+A)/A|=|D|=\frac{n}{|S_{0}|}, it follows that A∩(D−D)={0}.A\cap(D-D)=\{0\}. By Lemma 2.3, ℤn=S0⊕D.\mathbb{Z}_{n}=S_{0}\oplus D. Therefore, by Lemma 2.2, Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient dominating set D.D.  

4 Efficient open dominating sets

Now we turn to study efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphs.

Theorem 4.1

Let DD be a proper subset of ℤn\mathbb{Z}_{n} such that |D||D| divides nn and is relatively prime to n|D|.\frac{n}{|D|}. Then DD is an efficient open dominating set in some circulant graph Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) if and only if |D||D| is even and d−d′≢0​(m​o​d​|D|)d-d^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|D|) for any distinct d,d′∈D.d,d^{\prime}\in D.

Proof. If |D||D| is even and d−d′≢0​(m​o​d​|D|)d-d^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|D|) for any distinct d,d′∈D,d,d^{\prime}\in D, then ((n2+|D|​ℤn)−(n2+|D|​ℤn))∩(D−D)={0}.((\frac{n}{2}+|D|\mathbb{Z}_{n})-(\frac{n}{2}+|D|\mathbb{Z}_{n}))\cap(D-D)=\{0\}. Note that the cardinality of n2+|D|​ℤn\frac{n}{2}+|D|\mathbb{Z}_{n} is n|D|.\frac{n}{|D|}. Therefore, by Proposition 2.1, ℤn=(n2+|D|​ℤn)⊕D.\mathbb{Z}_{n}=(\frac{n}{2}+|D|\mathbb{Z}_{n})\oplus D. Set S=n2+|D|​ℤn.S=\frac{n}{2}+|D|\mathbb{Z}_{n}. Then SS is inverse-closed and ℤn=S⊕D.\mathbb{Z}_{n}=S\oplus D. Next we claim that 0∉S.0\notin S. Otherwise, if 0∈S,0\in S, then there exists some k∈{0,1,⋯,n|D|−1}k\in\{0,1,\cdots,\frac{n}{|D|}-1\} such that 0=n2+k​|D|,0=\frac{n}{2}+k|D|, and thus k​|D|=n2,k|D|=\frac{n}{2}, which implies that n|D|=2​k.\frac{n}{|D|}=2k. Therefore, |D||D| is not relatively prime to n|D|,\frac{n}{|D|}, which is a contradiction. By Lemma 2.2, DD is an efficient open dominating set in the circulant graph Cay​(ℤn,S).\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S).

If DD is an efficient open dominating set in Cay​(ℤn,S),\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S), then by the definition of an efficient open dominating set, it is easy to see that DD induces a matching in Cay​(ℤn,S),\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S), and thus |D||D| is even. Moreover, if DD is an efficient open dominating set in Cay​(ℤn,S),\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S), then by Lemma 2.6, ℤn=S⊕D.\mathbb{Z}_{n}=S\oplus D. Similar to the proof of the ‘only if’ part in Theorem 3.1, we can obtain that d−d′≢0​(m​o​d​|D|)d-d^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|D|) for any distinct d,d′∈D.d,d^{\prime}\in D.  

Using Lemmas 2.6 and 2.7 and following the proof of Theorem 3.2 but with S0S_{0} replaced by S,S, one can prove the following result, which also implies [7, Theorem 1.4] and [2, Theorems 5.4–5.6].

Theorem 4.2

Let SS be an inverse-closed subset of ℤn∖{0}\mathbb{Z}_{n}\setminus\{0\} such that |S||S| divides nn and |S||S| is relatively prime to n|S|.\frac{n}{|S|}. Then Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient open dominating set if and only if s−s′≢0​(m​o​d​|S|)s-s^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|S|) for distinct s,s′∈S.s,s^{\prime}\in S.

By Lemma 2.7 and Theorem 4.2, one can easily observe the following result.

Corollary 4.3

Let SS be an inverse-closed subset of ℤn∖{0}\mathbb{Z}_{n}\setminus\{0\} such that |S||S| divides nn and |S||S| is relatively prime to n|S|.\frac{n}{|S|}. Then Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) either doesn’t admit any efficient open dominating set or admits an efficient open dominating set which is a subgroup of ℤn.\mathbb{Z}_{n}.

Note that every finite abelian group is a direct product of some cyclic groups. By Lemma 2.6, we can obtain the following corollary which generalizes the result of Theorem 4.2 about circulant graphs by giving a similar result about Cayley graphs on abelian groups.

Corollary 4.4

Let GG be an abelian group and write G=ℤn1×⋯×ℤnk,G=\mathbb{Z}_{n_{1}}\times\cdots\times\mathbb{Z}_{n_{k}}, where kk and n1,⋯,nkn_{1},\cdots,n_{k} are positive integers, let S=S1×⋯×Sk,S=S_{1}\times\cdots\times S_{k}, where SiS_{i} is an inverse-closed subset of ℤni∖{0}\mathbb{Z}_{n_{i}}\setminus\{0\} such that |Si||S_{i}| divides nin_{i} and |Si||S_{i}| is relatively prime to ni|Si|\frac{n_{i}}{|S_{i}|} for each i∈{1,⋯,k}.i\in\{1,\cdots,k\}. Then Cay​(G,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(G,S) admits an efficient open dominating set if and only if si−si′≢0​(m​o​d​|Si|)s_{i}-s_{i}^{\prime}\nequiv 0~(mod~|S_{i}|) for distinct si,si′∈Sis_{i},s_{i}^{\prime}\in S_{i} and each i∈{1,⋯,k}.i\in\{1,\cdots,k\}.

Using Lemmas 2.4 and 2.6 and following the proof of Theorem 3.4 but with S0S_{0} replaced by SS, we can prove the following result.

Theorem 4.5

Suppose that Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) admits an efficient open dominating set. Then the set 𝔻\mathbb{D} of all efficient open dominating sets of Cay​(ℤn,S)\hbox{\rm Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_{n},S) satisfies the following (i)-(ii):

(i) {i+|S|ℤn:i=0,1,⋯,|S|−1}⊆𝔻⊆{{i+kin|S|:i=0,1,⋯,n|S|−1}:∀ki∈{0,1,⋯,|S|−1}};\{i+|S|\mathbb{Z}_{n}\colon\,i=0,1,\cdots,|S|-1\}\subseteq\mathbb{D}\subseteq\{\{i+k_{i}\frac{n}{|S|}\colon\,i=0,1,\cdots,\frac{n}{|S|}-1\}\colon\,\forall\,k_{i}{\in}\{0,1,\cdots,|S|{-}1\}\};

(ii) For any D∈𝔻,l∈ℤn,D\in\mathbb{D},\,l\in\mathbb{Z}_{n}, and any integer kk relatively prime to |D|,|D|, the set k​D+l∈𝔻.kD+l\in\mathbb{D}.
